transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-04
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Verdant Head of Platform), Daniel Lewis (Verdant CTO), Sofia Martinez (Verdant Partnerships)

Summary:
Introductory partner discovery between Redwood Inference and Verdant Infra to explore go-to-market and technical integration opportunities. Discussion covered Verdant's managed GPU offering, networking/VPC options, joint benchmark ideas, compliance needs (SOC2, SSO), and potential integration points (marketplace listing, dedicated capacity reseller). Next steps: share docs, schedule tech deep dive, and draft initial partner engagement model.

Topics:
- Verdant product overview and target customers
- Integration surface (API, marketplace, dedicated pooling)
- Security/compliance requirements (SOC 2, SAML, KMS)
- Technical constraints: networking, multi-tenancy, KV cache, quantization profiles
- Commercial partnership models and pilot criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Lena with Redwood, AE on the partnerships team. Marcus is our solutions engineer. How are you all doing?
[00:07] Priya Nair: Good thanks, excited to chat. We had a quick internal pre-brief, so we wanted to introduce Verdant Infra - we run managed GPU clusters and a marketplace for infra + managed stacks.
[00:18] Marcus Chen: Nice to meet you all. Quick call agenda - brief intros, Verdant overview, then dive a little on tech/integration points and compliance. Can that work?
[00:26] Daniel Lewis: Yep that's perfect. We're primarily interested in two things: 1) partnering on a marketplace listing where customers can spin up Redwood-backed inference, and 2) a technical reseller model for dedicated capacity where Verdant would host Redwood Dedicated under our private network.
[00:41] Lena Ortiz: Awesome. From Redwood's side we do hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Common integrations are marketplace images, terraform modules, and direct API integration for routing customers to dedicated pools.
[00:56] Sofia Martinez: For go-to-market, we focus on enterprise customers in finance and med-tech who need private deployments and strong audit controls. They ask about SOC2, SSO, and also regional data residency.
[01:12] Marcus Chen: Great context. From a technical lens, some things we care about: how networking will work (VPC peering, transit gateway, or private link), whether customers will want KMS/HSM integrations for keys, and what kinds of GPUs you expose (A100, H100, etc) and whether you've got support for quantized runtimes.
[01:31] Priya Nair: We run mixture of H100 and A100; in some regions customers prefer A100 due to availability. We can expose either and we have options for isolated tenants or shared multi-tenant pools.
[01:43] Daniel Lewis: On networking we typically do VPC peering for enterprise customers, but we can do private link endpoints as well if Redwood needs. We also have SAML SSO and can surface audit logs.
[01:54] Marcus Chen: That would cover a lot. For Redwood Dedicated we'd want to ensure we can manage model versions and routing, but the key is low-latency egress and the ability to run benchmarks under realistic load (we do continuous batching, KV cache, etc). Any constraints on running CPU-side tooling for benchmark harness?
[02:13] Priya Nair: CPU tooling in an isolated eval env is fine. We usually allocate ephemeral VMs for benchmarking. One ask: can Redwood produce a small benchmark script and a set of sample prompts so we can validate latency/cost claims?
[02:25] Lena Ortiz: Absolutely, Marcus can put together a benchmark plan with sample payloads and a short runner (bash/python) — we'll share it after this call.
[02:33] Daniel Lewis: Cool. A couple of security questions: our customers require SOC 2 Type II, encryption-in-transit and at-rest, and sometimes customer-managed keys. What does Redwood support?
[02:45] Marcus Chen: We support TLS everywhere, at-rest encryption, and for Private deployments we do KMS integrations and can support customer-managed keys via HSM in some cases. We also provide audit logs and RBAC in the Console. For hosted API we have SOC 2 compliance and can share the report under NDA.
[03:03] Sofia Martinez: Do you have any redactions or limitations in the SOC 2 report for partner review?
[03:09] Marcus Chen: Typically we provide the SOC 2 report via secure share and can redact customer-specific info; our security team can handle partner-level engagement.
[03:19] Priya Nair: For the marketplace listing, what's the usual integration level? Is it a turnkey image that customers deploy, or a managed service link to Redwood API?
[03:29] Lena Ortiz: Both patterns exist. Some partners prefer a 'click-to-deploy' image that includes agent + terraform to create Dedicated pools; others prefer an integration where the marketplace links to Redwood's hosted API and we route calls to partner-hosted Dedicated instances. The choice often depends on privacy and latency requirements.
[03:46] Daniel Lewis: For enterprise accounts wanting air-gapped or on-prem, can Redwood ship a package?
[03:50] Marcus Chen: Yes, our Private offering supports on-prem packaging and enterprise licensing. It requires some integration work but we've done it with a few customers.
[03:58] Priya Nair: Great. On billing/commercials — we typically either take a cut on marketplace sales or run a reseller pricing where we wholesale capacity. What's Redwood's preference?
[04:08] Lena Ortiz: We're flexible. For initial pilots many partners prefer a revenue-share or referral fee. For Dedicated/reseller we usually do a capacity-based wholesale contract. We'll draft a couple of models and share.
[04:19] Sofia Martinez: Any concerns from Redwood about shared multi-tenant pools vs dedicated?
[04:23] Marcus Chen: For model security and customer isolation, Dedicated is preferred for enterprise; shared pools are fine for smaller customers. Also performance SLOs are easier to guarantee on Dedicated.
[04:34] Daniel Lewis: On the tech side, what's the smallest run you'd recommend to validate latency? We were thinking 99th p99 latency under 300ms for 8k context requests, but that may be unrealistic.
[04:46] Marcus Chen: 8k context and 300ms p99 is extremely aggressive, depends on model and GPU. For typical open models on H100 we can aim for 200-400ms for shorter sequences, but for 8k sequences you should expect higher latency. For those workloads we recommend model-optimized kernels and quantization profiles — we can recommend model variants. We'll propose a benchmark matrix.
[05:10] Priya Nair: That helps. On quota and autoscale — customers want predictable capacity for peak times. Do you have autoscaling hooks that integrate with provider APIs?
[05:20] Marcus Chen: Yes, Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. We can wire autoscaling to Verdant's orchestration via APIs. We also support graceful fallback policies to lower-cost variants if Dedicated capacity is saturated.
[05:34] Lena Ortiz: I'd like to capture potential integration touchpoints: 1) Marketplace listing + click-to-deploy, 2) Dedicated reseller (wholesale capacity), 3) Joint benchmark + case study, 4) Security exchange + partner onboarding. Are we aligned?
[05:48] Priya Nair: Yes that aligns. Also we have a set of SI partners who could help integration for large customers; we'll loop them in when appropriate.
[05:57] Daniel Lewis: A question on telemetry — our customers need certain audit events forwarded to their SIEM. Can Redwood stream logs or provide an agent?
[06:07] Marcus Chen: We can forward logs via secure syslog or S3 export and provide trace hooks in Console. For Private we can integrate directly into customer SIEMs. We'll need to map events and retention.
[06:19] Sofia Martinez: Any limitations on model licensing? Some ISVs are concerned about open model redistribution when bundled in marketplace images.
[06:26] Lena Ortiz: Licensing differs by model; we maintain a model catalog and will flag models with redistribution restrictions. For marketplace images we typically include only redistributable model variants or provide links to pull model weights at deploy time under the partner's license.
[06:43] Priya Nair: Ok that makes sense. Another small ask: can Redwood provide a short partner FAQ for our sales team — "what questions to ask customers" and a one-pager on integration options?
[06:55] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we'll include a partner one-pager and FAQ with the deck.
[07:00] Marcus Chen: I'll also note technical pre-reqs: VPC peering/private link details, firewall ports, recommended GPU instance types, and benchmark script.
[07:11] Daniel Lewis: Sounds good. Anything else on SLAs? Our large customers sometimes require an uptime SLA and latency SLOs written into contracts.
[07:20] Lena Ortiz: For Dedicated and Private we offer SLA-backed contracts; we can propose target uptime and latency SLOs in the pilot agreement. For hosted API we have tiered SLAs.
[07:31] Priya Nair: Perfect.
[07:33] Sofia Martinez: Timeline-wise, what would a pilot look like? We were thinking a 6-8 week pilot: week 1-2 onboarding, week 3-4 bench and tuning, week 5-6 joint validation and go/no-go. Does Redwood have a standard pilot cadence?
[07:48] Marcus Chen: That timeline matches our experience. We'll prepare a milestone plan in the benchmark doc.
[07:55] Daniel Lewis: One final technical nit — you mentioned KV cache and prefix caching earlier, how does Redwood handle shared KV in multi-tenant setups?
[08:05] Marcus Chen: We partition KV cache per customer/tenant, and Dedicated provides isolated caches. For shared pools we tag cache entries with tenant IDs to avoid leakage. We'll document design patterns.
[08:18] Priya Nair: Good to know.
[08:20] Lena Ortiz: Alright I'll summarize next steps: Marcus will send benchmark script + plan; I'll send partner deck + one-pager and partner FAQ; Priya will send workload profile; Verdant will share SOC 2 and network details. We'll schedule a tech deep dive next week. Any objections?
[08:38] Daniel Lewis: None. Sounds good.
[08:40] Priya Nair: All good.
[08:41] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone — looking forward to working together.
[08:44] Sofia Martinez: Thanks, bye.

Recap / Notes:
- Integration patterns: marketplace image, hosted API link, Dedicated reseller, Private on-prem
- Technical pre-reqs: VPC peering or private link, KMS support for customer-managed keys, audit log export options, recommended GPUs (H100/A100), benchmark harness
- Compliance: Redwood provides SOC 2 report; Private supports HSM/KMS for CMKs
- Commercial: flexible (rev-share, reseller wholesale, pilot terms)

Links mentioned:
- Redwood partner deck (to be shared)
- Benchmark repo / sample prompts (to be shared)
- SOC 2 report (secure share under NDA)

End of transcript.
